# Domain models that protect rules and serve useful reads

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `architecture-ddd-cqrs` · **Architecture & Distributed Systems** · Catalog level: architect

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q034](#S04-Q034)

<p>What are an Aggregate and its Aggregate Root? Use one business invariant to explain how you would choose their boundary and allow changes.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Derive a domain model and read/write responsibilities from business meaning and invariants.</p>

<ul>
<li>Use shared terminology while making context-specific meaning explicit.</li>
<li>Trace a business invariant through an aggregate change and its event contract.</li>
<li>Justify separate read/write models or defend a simpler alternative.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Dependency direction and service ownership](architecture-boundaries.md)

<p>Start with the business problem and the language used to describe it. Identify where that meaning applies, then examine how a change preserves a rule and becomes an event. With those responsibilities clear, assess whether separate read and write models solve a real mismatch.</p>

<a id="S04-Q031"></a>

### S04-Q031 · Foundation

<p>What problem does Domain-Driven Design try to solve? Use a business rule that is hard to express consistently to explain when the approach would be useful.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q031](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q031)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q031](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q031)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What problem does Domain-Driven Design attempt to solve?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Connect modeling choices to understanding the business. Explain the problem first, before selecting tactical patterns or framework support.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Relate domain modeling to business complexity and communication.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic rule; distinguish complex business behavior from complexity caused only by traffic or infrastructure.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain how a shared model would change implementation decisions.</li>
<li>Describe a situation where the modeling effort would not be justified.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Defining DDD as a collection of entity, repository and service classes.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you ask a domain expert before writing the model?</li>
<li>How would you notice that the model no longer matches the business?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q032"></a>

### S04-Q032 · Foundation

<p>What does Ubiquitous Language mean in a domain model? Show how a business term would be used consistently in discussion, code and tests.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q032](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q032)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q032](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q032)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Ubiquitous Language.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>The question asks how a team gives a term a shared meaning. Explain what happens when everyday language hides different business rules.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Make business terminology precise enough to guide implementation.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose a generic term such as order or reservation; define the context and avoid assuming it means the same thing everywhere.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect the term to observable behavior and a concrete test.</li>
<li>Explain how disagreement or a changed meaning would update the model.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a vocabulary document as sufficient while code uses a different meaning.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you resolve two teams using the same word differently?</li>
<li>What test would expose an ambiguous definition?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q033"></a>

### S04-Q033 · Foundation

<p>What is a Bounded Context, and how would you recognize one in a business workflow? Explain what should happen when information crosses into another context.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q033](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q033)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q033](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q033)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Bounded Context.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Focus on where a model and its terms apply. Distinguish a semantic boundary from automatically choosing a new deployment unit.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Identify model boundaries and explicit integration meaning.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose two generic business contexts; clarify team and data ownership without assuming each context must be a microservice.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Show a term whose meaning differs across contexts and explain the consequence.</li>
<li>Describe an integration contract and how to test that it preserves the intended meaning.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating each Bounded Context with exactly one service or database.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Can two contexts live in the same application?</li>
<li>How would a change in one context&#x27;s model affect the integration?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q036"></a>

### S04-Q036 · Foundation

<p>What does CQRS separate, and what does that separation require in a simple application? Describe the read and write responsibilities without assuming separate databases.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q036](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q036)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q036](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q036)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What is CQRS?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Expand Command Query Responsibility Segregation through a concrete operation. Explain the responsibility split before choosing a storage or event architecture.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Define CQRS at its responsibility boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic update and read; clarify whether both paths share storage. Event sourcing and asynchronous projections are not assumed.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguish the responsibilities with a concrete read and state-changing command.</li>
<li>Explain which additional architecture choices are separate decisions.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating CQRS with event sourcing or requiring two databases in every design.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Could both responsibilities use one database?</li>
<li>What would a reader observe if a separate projection has not caught up?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q034"></a>

### S04-Q034 · Mechanism

<p>What are an Aggregate and its Aggregate Root? Use one business invariant to explain how you would choose their boundary and allow changes.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q034](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q034)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q034](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q034)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Aggregate and Aggregate Root.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>An invariant is a rule that must remain true. Focus on which related state must be protected together rather than grouping objects by convenient navigation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about a consistency boundary from a business invariant.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose a generic rule and state concurrency assumptions. Distinguish the domain boundary from ORM loading and physical table layout.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace a state change and explain which rule must still hold.</li>
<li>Discuss contention or boundary size and a test involving competing changes.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Making every reachable object part of one aggregate because the ORM can load it.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if a rule seems to span two aggregates?</li>
<li>How would concurrent requests challenge the proposed invariant?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q035"></a>

### S04-Q035 · Mechanism

<p>What makes an event a Domain Event? Describe a business transition and explain what an interested component needs to understand about that event.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q035](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q035)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q035](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q035)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Domain Events.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Separate a meaningful business fact from a low-level change notification. Clarify the event contract and the point at which it becomes valid.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Express a business transition through an explicit event contract.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose a generic transition; distinguish an in-process event from a published integration event and state the commit boundary.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect event meaning to an actual business transition and relevant data.</li>
<li>Trace what happens if publication or consumer processing fails.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating every database update as a useful domain event without explaining its meaning.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Should an external consumer receive the same representation as an internal handler?</li>
<li>How would you evolve the event without changing its meaning unexpectedly?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q037"></a>

### S04-Q037 · Application

<p>When would separate read and write models help a system? Describe one mismatch between the two workloads and how you would test whether separation is worthwhile.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q037](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q037)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q037](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q037)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When does separating read and write models help?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A read model serves information needs; a write model protects state changes. Explain the difficulty caused by using one representation before proposing another.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Justify model separation using a concrete workload and validation.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State query shape, update rules and freshness requirements. Separate models need not imply separate storage or asynchronous delivery.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Relate the proposed models to different user and correctness needs.</li>
<li>Compare a simpler alternative and evidence for benefits and synchronization costs.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing two models simply because CQRS is an architectural goal.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What freshness contract would the read side expose?</li>
<li>What would you measure before adding a separate projection?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q038"></a>

### S04-Q038 · Trade-offs

<p>When would CQRS introduce more complexity than value? Describe a simpler design you would keep and the evidence that would make you reconsider.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q038](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q038)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q038](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q038)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When is CQRS unnecessary complexity?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Evaluate the actual responsibility split and any extra projection or synchronization work. The decision depends on the problem, not the pattern&#x27;s popularity.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reject unnecessary model separation with defensible criteria.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State business complexity, read/write needs and team capacity; distinguish lightweight separation from a distributed projection architecture.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain why the simpler design satisfies the present requirements.</li>
<li>Name a changed requirement that would justify a deeper separation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating either universal adoption or universal rejection of CQRS as sound judgment.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which additional failure path would a separate read store introduce?</li>
<li>How could you retain a useful responsibility split without extra infrastructure?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>For a reservation service, a customer requests several seats while availability is also read by a dashboard. Define the business terms, the rule governing concurrent reservations and the model boundary. Describe the event meaning and decide whether a separate dashboard model is warranted, including its freshness contract and a simpler alternative.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Defines the main concepts and gives a consistent business example.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Connects context, invariant and event meaning to implementation boundaries and a justified read/write choice.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Pattern vocabulary without a state-change trace, competing-change test or read freshness contract does not show model validity.</p>
